subject: Reliability / SLO follow-up and proposed test plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Reliability / SLO follow-up and proposed test plan

Hi Alex — great chat earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:  

1) Summary of what we heard from you on today’s call:
- Primary concern: predictable availability and graceful degradation during regional incidents.
- Current baseline: using Hyperscaler-X endpoints for model inference; average 95th latency ~180ms for 1K RPS but customers see spikes during deployments/maintenance.
- Rate limits: you currently hit soft throttles at sustained bursts >1.2k RPS and have seen 429s during peak spikes; net effect is queuing and occasional user-facing errors.

2) Where Redwood can help (high level):
- Dedicated pools (reserved capacity) with explicit SLOs and error budgets for critical paths.
- Fast failover: cross-region routing + immediate fallback to quantized-compatible model variant to keep tail latency bounded when worker nodes fail.
- Transparent rate limiting and per-route quotas (we can set customer-specific burst tokens to avoid 429s on short spikes).
- Observability: token-level latency/cost breakdowns + per-request traces to diagnose degraded responses.

3) Proposed tests we discussed (to validate reliability guarantees):
- Sustained load: 60-minute soak at 1k RPS with synthetic payloads similar to your prod distribution (measure 50/95/99 latencies, error rate).
- Spike test: 30s -> 5s ramp to 2k RPS to observe buffer/backpressure and any 429 behavior.
- Chaos failover: take one region offline and validate cross-region routing and KV-cache warmup behavior (measure warmup latency impact on first 500 tokens).
- Error-budget burn validation: intentionally inject 2% transient error rate to observe automatic fallback and alerting behavior.

Attachments: I’m attaching a draft SLO comparison sheet (slo-comparison.xlsx) that maps Redwood vs Hyperscaler-X vs other APIs across uptime, rate limits, error budgets, and failover modes.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm which endpoints/regions you want included in the soak and chaos tests? (us-west-2 and us-east-1 suggested)
- Do you have an existing traffic replay or sample payload set we can use? If not, we can generate a synthetic set matching your percentile distribution.
- If you’re comfortable, we can schedule the initial soak for next Tuesday (Mar 16) during your low-traffic window.

I’ll follow up internally to line up an engineer for test execution and an SRE to observe metrics.

Thanks — Ben

Marissa / Rishi — summary and ask from ACME call (for our SRE/runbook + SE pairing):

What they need:
- Reliability validation vs Hyperscaler-X (esp. failover behavior and 429s during spikes).
- Clear SLOs and a recommended error-budget policy for two tiers (prod-critical, prod-standard).

Recommended Redwood approach (high level):
- Prod-critical: 99.95% monthly uptime, 99th latency target < 250ms (for their model payload), 0.1% sustained error budget; automatic region failover with warm KV cache strategy + fallback to quantized model variant in 2–5s window.
- Prod-standard: 99.9% monthly uptime, 99th latency target < 350ms, 0.5% error budget; best-effort warmup on failover, longer KV-cache warmup.

Technical notes for test leads:
- For chaos failover: ensure ingress DNS TTL and our routing policy force immediate reroute; capture pre/post histograms for first 15 mins.
- For spike test: measure 429 pattern (burst tokens granted) and whether our burst token bucket prevents client-side 429s.
- Observability: enable per-request tracing + sample token-level cost breakdown to compare cost delta vs Hyperscaler-X.

Attachments: proposal-notes.pdf (internal notes, 8KB)

Can you own the chaos test run (Rishi) and Marissa can you coordinate with solutions/devrel to prepare the synthetic replay if ACME doesn’t provide? I’ll own the test plan and outcome writeup.

Ben

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming regions. We’re good to schedule the soak on Tue Mar 16. Below is the concise test plan and expected deliverables.

Test plan (confirmed):
- Soak (Tue Mar 16, 02:00–03:00 PDT): 1,000 RPS sustained for 60 minutes across us-west-2/us-east-1 split as you described. Deliverables: latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), error rate, throughput, Pod/queue metrics.
- Spike (Tue Mar 16, 03:15–03:45 PDT): ramp to 2k RPS for 30s bursts, repeat 6x. Deliverables: 429 incidence, burst token utilization, tail-latency impact.
- Chaos (Tue Mar 16, 04:30–05:00 PDT): region failover exercise (take us-west-2 simulated outage). Deliverables: successful failover time, cache-warmup latency for first 500 tokens, dropped request count.

Answers to your questions:  
1) In-flight requests: by default we will attempt to gracefully drain and retry where safe. For model inference requests that are idempotent we will retry once automatically; for non-idempotent flows we’ll surface errors and rely on your retry logic. During a hard failover there may be a small window (a few seconds) where the first requests hit a cold cache and latency increases — that’s why we recommend the quantized fallback path to keep tail latency bounded.

2) Error-budget policy: see short guidance below and we’ll formalize in the follow-up doc:
- Prod-critical: 0.1% monthly budget. Automated alerting at 25% burn and runbook for mitigation at 50% burn. If burn > 75% during maintenance window, auto-scale and route to second-tier capacity.
- Prod-standard: 0.5% monthly budget. Alerting at 50% burn.

I’ve attached a short whitepaper that includes our recommended policies and a side-by-side SLO comparison vs Hyperscaler-X (redwood-whitepaper.pdf). I also added links to a HubSpot deal note and a draft DocuSign for a POC order if you want to accelerate procurement: 
- HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8341

- DocuSign (POC): https://www.docusign.com/en/DEMO-ACME-POC
